page: Vultr voc-m-16c-128gb-3200s-amd is an instance within the Optimized Cloud Compute family, configured with dedicated AMD EPYC x86_64 processors. The instance provides 16 vCPUs derived from 8 physical cores running at 2.0 GHz with two threads per core. Cache configuration includes 32 KB L1 data cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. Memory allocation totals 128.0 GB of RAM, yielding an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio. Storage consists of a bundled 3200 GB NVMe SSD, accompanied by one complimentary public IPv4 address. No dedicated hardware GPUs are attached to this configuration.

Benchmark results highlight strong memory subsystem metrics and robust single-core compute performance. The system achieved a top-tier stress-ng single-core score of 3133.97 and a top-tier PassMark memory score of 2992.99. Large-block memory bandwidth demonstrated sustained throughput in the top 25%, delivering 340.0 GB/sec for uncached reads and 160.84 GB/sec for writes. Multi-core compute benchmarks positioned firmly within the median range, showing a Geekbench multi-core score of 13414.0 and a multi-threaded stress-ng score of 50113.61. CPU-based machine learning inference on small models reached 315.31 tokens/sec for text generation, while medium model generation maintained 25.41 tokens/sec.

The 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio combined with high-capacity NVMe storage creates an efficient deployment footprint for memory-bound and I/O-intensive workloads without paying for high-core licenses or unutilized processing capacity. The hardware profile lacks AVX-512 extensions and advanced matrix accelerators, meaning heavily vectorized computational tasks rely on standard AVX execution. Workloads that align with this instance profile include relational database engines, high-capacity in-memory caches, large-scale Redis deployments, and data warehousing tasks requiring rapid local NVMe throughput.

Network-facing applications benefit from stable web throughput, recorded at 15.74 GB/sec for static serving, alongside Redis SET performance reaching 38.03 million operations per second. The server balances high storage density and generous RAM capacity with dedicated core stability, serving as an effective node for enterprise backend systems, ETL data transformation pipelines, and persistent database hosting.

It features an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio and lacks dedicated GPU accelerators. Benchmark evaluation indicates top-tier memory performance with a PassMark memory score of 2992.99 and strong uncached read bandwidth reaching 340.0 GB/sec. With extensive NVMe capacity and substantial memory density, it is well-suited for hosting memory-intensive applications, operational relational databases, caching layers, and medium-scale data analytics pipelines.
